instructions: Rinse 1 1/2 cups of rice until the water runs mostly clear. Cook it with 3 cups of water, covered, until each grain is separate and tender. Check the package for the time.
Spread the rice on a large plate or tray and let it cool completely. It mixes better when it's cool and dry.
Meanwhile, put the tamarind in a bowl with the jaggery and 1 cup of hot water. Leave it for 15 minutes.
Squeeze the tamarind with your fingers until it breaks down, then press the liquid through a strainer into a bowl. Throw away the fibers and seeds.
Make the spice powder. Heat a dry pan over medium-low heat. Add 1 tbsp of the chana dal, 1 tbsp of the urad dal and 2 of the dried red chilies, and stir for 2 minutes, until the dals are light gold.
Add the coriander seeds, cumin seeds, fenugreek seeds, 1/2 tsp of the mustard seeds and the black pepper. Stir for 1 minute, until they smell toasty.
Add the sesame seeds and coconut and stir for 30 seconds, until the coconut is pale gold. Stir in half of the asafoetida, then transfer everything to a plate and let it cool for 5 minutes.
Grind it to a fine powder in a spice grinder.
Heat the sesame oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Add the remaining 1/2 tsp mustard seeds. After about 20 seconds they will start to pop. That's your cue for the next step.
Add the peanuts and the remaining 1 tbsp chana dal and 1 tbsp urad dal. Stir for 1 to 2 minutes, until the peanuts and dals are golden.
Add the remaining dried red chili, broken in half, the curry leaves and the rest of the asafoetida. Stand back a little. The leaves will spatter. Stir for 15 seconds.
Pour in the tamarind liquid, then add the turmeric and 1 tsp of the salt. Simmer over medium heat for 10 to 12 minutes, until it's thick and the oil starts to separate at the edges.
Stir in the spice powder, a little at a time. Cook for 2 minutes, until it's a thick paste, adding a splash of water if it gets stiff.
Add the paste to the cooled rice a few spoonfuls at a time, folding gently so the grains stay whole. Stop when every grain is coated. You may not need all of it.
Sprinkle over the last 1/2 tsp salt, taste it, and add a pinch more if it's flat. Cover and leave it for 30 minutes.

Serve at room temperature, with yogurt or papad if you have them. Packed in a lunch box, it keeps in the fridge for up to 2 days. Eat it cold or at room temperature, or microwave it for about 1 minute.
method_notes: Swasthi's and Hebbar's agree on cooked short-grain rice cooled before mixing, a tamarind paste with peanuts, dals and curry leaves, and a roasted spice powder stirred in, then a rest so the rice takes on the flavor. They differ in that Hebbar's makes a big jar of gojju (a paste that keeps a month) and uses more oil and chilies, while Swasthi's makes just enough paste for one batch. The app's rating rule makes Hebbar's the lead, but its jar-sized gojju batch was scaled down using Swasthi's single-batch amounts, scaled up for 4 and with the dried chilies cut back to keep it mild. Swasthi's page showed only a visible rating (5 from 81 votes), not the JSON-LD; Hebbar's shows 4.98 from 193 votes.
